presentation.label: Micro timing for the whole track
presentation.summary: TRACK TRIG EDIT row MICRO T. LEVEL sets every step on the selected audio or MIDI track to that micro timing.
presentation.overview: FUNC+BANK TRACK TRIG EDIT gains MICRO T under TRIGS. LEVEL rewrites every step of the selected track through the stock micro-timing writer. MIDI button off writes the audio track. MIDI button on writes the MIDI track only.
highlights: The window stays four rows. REC.TRG scrolls in below SWING.
LEVEL applies as it turns. There is no YES to confirm.
Audio and MIDI keep separate trigs. The footer uses the stock fraction.
usage: Grid record, then FUNC+BANK (FUNCTION on MKI). Highlight MICRO T, under TRIGS.
Turn LEVEL. The footer fraction moves, and every step on this track takes that micro timing.
Press the MIDI button and turn LEVEL again to set the MIDI track. The audio track keeps the value it already had.

controls.name: MICRO T
controls.doc: Index 23 is on grid (0). 0 is -23 and 46 is +23, in stock micro-timing steps. LEVEL writes that absolute value to every step of the side on screen.

limitations: OS 1.40C. The LEVEL behaviour was reported on a private MICRO T9 card. This package's USB Keep and power-cycle footer are in TESTING.md. The pictures are this package on a development twin, and they are not a unit result.

One byte is kept per bank, the pattern on the screen, and track, in this module's unit. Audio and MIDI share it. A power cycle drops the unit, so the row starts on grid again. It is not battery RAM and it is not stored in the project. Rewritten trigs stay in the pattern.
The next LEVEL turn sets all 64 steps, including empty ones. An individual trig edit does not move the row.

storage.label: ColdFire unit and its UI-stack peak
storage.conditions: Package f5b9682175f295875dbecb66a18524c205ba526d88e9bd7dc9cdd7d270d01292. Linked image 1076 bytes (1030 of code, the MICRO T label, a 16-byte footer buffer, the centre 0 and a 20-byte name table) plus 2048 bytes of bss. A LEVEL rewrite pushes 64 bytes on the UI stack. No heap and no DSP memory. The stock writer's own stack is not in the number.

processing.label: ColdFire, while LEVEL turns on MICRO T
processing.conditions: ot_emu PC watch of the 1076-byte image, 19 November 2026. One LEVEL step with the MIDI button on was 788 instructions of this module. The audio side was 787. The stock 64-step writer is not in the number.

impact.conditions: LEVEL on the MICRO T row writes 64 trigs through the stock setter. Other rows jump back to stock.

cpu.rationale: One pot turn walks all 64 steps through the stock writer. No per-audio-frame work.

dsp.rationale: No DSP code. Playback uses the trig words the stock writer stored.

memory.rationale: 3188 bytes: 1076 in the linked image, 2048 for the remembered row, and 64 on the UI stack while LEVEL rewrites. The loader clears the row when the module loads. A power cycle drops the unit. No battery RAM, no heap and no DSP memory.

cpuPrice.conditions: MKII, OS 1.40C, development twin 878307834ad3c23a RAM-booted (no controller rows, not flashed). Package f5b9682175f295875dbecb66a18524c205ba526d88e9bd7dc9cdd7d270d01292 of commit dbc0652b4, built before this twin. One 8 s reading, pattern left as the unit came up, transport stopped beforehand, module installed and LEVEL not turning. Frame interrupt +0.0 points. The CPU meter read +0.9 and is not this price.

tests.summary: Author reported the private MICRO T9 card working for audio and MIDI separately. Headless ot_emu captured TRACK TRIG EDIT: MICRO T on grid, +1/384 after LEVEL, MIDI page, and REC.TRG scrolled into the four-row window. From 0.1.1 the remembered row is module bss (mt_table). On 18 November 2026 package f5b9682175f295875dbecb66a18524c205ba526d88e9bd7dc9cdd7d270d01292 was kept over USB on an MKII; after a power cycle the person reported the footer on grid. Shipped catalogue package 8958a66f2942e4e0c5692c0cf075bab3c07e4f3347d716ac57405b1792cb6c47 matches that ColdFire image; title field only differs.

conditions.parameterExtremes: MICRO T selected; LEVEL stepped on the audio side (787) and with the MIDI button on (788). The dearest counted event is one MIDI-side LEVEL step from mt_level back to stock.
conditions.parameterModulation: No LFO, p-lock, MIDI CC or scene reaches this module. LEVEL on the MICRO T row is the only control that runs the rewrite.
conditions.modeSwitching: Twenty LEVEL steps with the MIDI button on: ten while playing, STOP, Part change 1→2, page opened again, ten more while playing. The remembered byte moved 0x02→0x0c→0x16.
conditions.maxLoad: One instance. No track voice, FX slot or DSP core. The count is this module's instructions only; the stock 64-step writer at 0x4002d640 is not in the number.
conditions.inputConditions: ot_emu PC watch on every halfword of the 1076-byte image, development twin 878307834ad3c23a, package f5b9682175f295875dbecb66a18524c205ba526d88e9bd7dc9cdd7d270d01292 (ColdFire image identical to the shipped package; title field only differs). Transport playing, set OCTABAM, project ONEAUX, pattern 0. Executed instructions, not chip wall-clock.

memory.conditions: ABI 7 package 8958a66f2942e4e0c5692c0cf075bab3c07e4f3347d716ac57405b1792cb6c47 (2926 B, module 36200ffc): linked image 1076 bytes (1030 code + label/footer/glyph/name table) and 2048 bytes of bss (mt_table). Image SHA-256 08b92351ea2097a9b26578eeebe72968b22df25c650f2a60fbcdd816bc103fbc. A LEVEL rewrite pushes 64 bytes on the UI stack. No heap, no battery RAM, no DSP memory. Hardware canaries were not measured. Keep Accept on 18 November 2026 used package f5b9682175f295875dbecb66a18524c205ba526d88e9bd7dc9cdd7d270d01292, which differs only in the 16-byte title field (Micro Timing pe → Micro Timing); ColdFire image and module id match.

hardware.summary: On a MKII, OS 1.40C, flashed base 931a91bd7e571216, package f5b9682175f295875dbecb66a18524c205ba526d88e9bd7dc9cdd7d270d01292 (title Micro Timing pe; ColdFire image identical to shipped 8958a66f2942e4e0c5692c0cf075bab3c07e4f3347d716ac57405b1792cb6c47) was kept with --accept beside 22 modules already on the card. After a power cycle the inventory still listed Micro Timing (module 36200ffc) and the person reported footer MT1:ON GRID. Removal while TRACK TRIG EDIT's key layer was open was refused (loader 11 RUNTIME_UI_OPEN); after a second power cycle with menus closed, remove --accept cleared it. Author also reported LEVEL behaviour on private MICRO T9 card (different image).
limitations: Keep Accept used package f5b9682175f295875dbecb66a18524c205ba526d88e9bd7dc9cdd7d270d01292; the shipped catalogue package is 8958a66f2942e4e0c5692c0cf075bab3c07e4f3347d716ac57405b1792cb6c47. They differ only in the 16-byte title field; ColdFire image 08b92351ea2097a9b26578eeebe72968b22df25c650f2a60fbcdd816bc103fbc and module id 36200ffc match.
LEVEL audio/MIDI separation on this package was not a hardware pass; the development-twin trial was Undo-only and is not a LEVEL pass.
An MKI was not tried. A card flash of this package was not tried.
Part save and project save of the remembered row do not apply: the row lives in module bss and clears on load/power-cycle.
LCD captures in media/ are headless ot_emu frames, not unit photographs.
Cycle counts are emulator executed instructions, not chip wall-clock.

steps: Grid record, then FUNC+BANK (FUNCTION on MKI). Highlight MICRO T, under TRIGS.
Turn LEVEL. The footer fraction moves, and every step on this track takes that micro timing.
Press the MIDI button and turn LEVEL again to set the MIDI track. The audio track keeps the value it already had.

license.declaration: Original module by jonathanwardle1992-beep, MIT. No firmware, extracted stock code or built images are included.

media.caption: While grid recording, press FUNC+BANK (FUNCTION on MKI) and highlight MICRO T under TRIGS. The pictured row is still on grid: the cursor sits on the centre 0 and the footer reads MT1:ON GRID. Turn LEVEL on this row to write that fraction to every step.
media.alt: TRACK TRIG EDIT with MICRO T highlighted under TRIGS, a dashed lane and a cursor on the centre mark, footer MT1:ON GRID.

otUi.setup: Headless ot_emu; MKII panel; stopped transport; 128×64 LCD at integer scale 6; DSP cores running. Development twin 5e359bf64919555125f0225744b5bb886a5661bed0e00279065b7ea38f99597b. Package f5b9682175f295875dbecb66a18524c205ba526d88e9bd7dc9cdd7d270d01292 installed over the emulator USB link and not kept. YES, REC, FUNC+BANK, DOWN onto MICRO T. Grayscale 24 and 240. Not a hardware result.

media.caption: With MICRO T highlighted, turn LEVEL one step. The cursor moves one mark to the right of the centre 0 and the footer reads MT1:+1/384. That fraction is what a LEVEL turn on this row writes to the track.
media.alt: TRACK TRIG EDIT with MICRO T highlighted, the cursor one step right of centre, footer MT1:+1/384.

otUi.setup: Same session as ot-micro-t.png. One LEVEL +1 after that frame. The remembered byte moved from 0 to 1. Not a hardware result.

media.caption: Press the MIDI button. The title becomes MIDI TRIG EDIT and SLIDE leaves the list. MICRO T stays highlighted and the footer still reads MT1:+1/384, the value already on the row. Turn LEVEL on this page to write the MIDI track.
media.alt: MIDI TRIG EDIT with MICRO T highlighted, SLIDE absent, footer MT1:+1/384.

otUi.setup: Same session. MIDI pressed once after the LEVEL step. LEVEL was not turned again, so the footer is still the audio step. Not a hardware result.

media.caption: Press MIDI again to leave the MIDI page, then DOWN until the list scrolls. TRIGS leaves the top and REC.TRG is highlighted on the bottom row. MICRO T, SLIDE and SWING stay above it, and the MICRO T lane still shows the cursor from the LEVEL step.
media.alt: TRACK TRIG EDIT scrolled so MICRO T, SLIDE and SWING sit above a highlighted REC.TRG row. TRIGS is off the top.

otUi.setup: Same session. MIDI pressed again, then three DOWN presses. Not a hardware result.
